1. `FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv_coeIdeal` (lines 24–32): the two branches each close with the same three-lemma `rw`. This is routine unfolding inside one proof, and a helper would only move the branch inside.

It is a two-line identity (the self-canonical equivalence acts trivially on units) inside a single proof. Factoring it out would save very little, so I did not report it.
3. `ClassGroup.mulEquiv_refl_apply` and `ClassGroup.mulEquiv_trans_apply` (lines 86–106): both use the same skeleton: `obtain` via `mk0_surjective`, rewrite with `mulEquiv_mk0`, `congr 1`, `Subtype.ext`, then a short ideal-map identity (`Ideal.map_id` or `Ideal.map_map`). The ideal-map calculations differ, and the shared skeleton is routine. A helper would be a thin wrapper.
4. `clEndHom` (`map_one'` and `map_mul'`): both prove equality of linear maps by `LinearMap.ext`, `clProj_surjective` and a `show`, then apply `mulEquiv_refl_apply` or `mulEquiv_trans_apply`. The mathematical content already sits in those lemmas, so this is plain structure-field boilerplate.
5. `clEnd_clProj_mk0` and `clGalAction_clProj_mk0`: the second just applies the first, so it is a thin wrapper.

I did not search other files for further duplication, because the rubric concerns repetition within or across proofs and the in-file candidates were all short. I am fairly confident in this verdict.
